misconceptions.name: Writes the ratio in the wrong order
misconceptions.feedback: You have the right numbers, but in the opposite order. In a ratio, the quantity named first in the question comes first.
misconceptions.next_action: Read the question again, find which quantity is named first, and put it on the left of the colon.

misconceptions.name: Compares a part with the total instead of with the other part
misconceptions.feedback: It looks like you compared one group with the total. This question compares one group with the other group.
misconceptions.next_action: Find the two groups the question names, and use only those two numbers.

misconceptions.name: Compares quantities in different units
misconceptions.feedback: The two quantities are in different units, so they can't be compared directly yet.
misconceptions.next_action: Change both quantities to the same unit first, then write the ratio.

misconceptions.name: Gives an equivalent ratio that is not in simplest form
misconceptions.feedback: Your ratio has the right value, but it can still be simplified. Both terms share a common factor.
misconceptions.next_action: Divide both terms by their HCF so they have no common factor other than 1.

misconceptions.name: Adds the same number to both terms instead of multiplying
misconceptions.feedback: It looks like you added the same amount to both terms. Equivalent ratios come from multiplying or dividing both terms by the same number.
misconceptions.next_action: Work out what one term was multiplied by, then multiply the other term by the same number.

misconceptions.name: Divides or multiplies by the wrong quantity in the unitary method
misconceptions.feedback: The steps are mixed up: the answer came from dividing by the wrong quantity.
misconceptions.next_action: First find the value of one item by dividing the total by the number of items, then multiply.

objectives.title: Compare two quantities by division and write the ratio in the right order

questions.prompt: A class has 12 girls and 18 boys. What is the ratio of girls to boys, in simplest form?
hints: The question names girls first, so the number of girls goes first: $12 : 18$.
Divide both terms by their HCF. What is the HCF of 12 and 18?
questions.solution: Girls to boys is $12 : 18$. The HCF of 12 and 18 is 6, so $12 : 18 = 2 : 3$.

questions.prompt: A box has 5 red pens and 7 blue pens. Write the ratio of blue pens to red pens.
hints: Which colour does the question name first?
Blue pens come first, so the ratio starts with 7.
questions.solution: Blue pens to red pens is $7 : 5$. 7 and 5 have no common factor, so it is already in simplest form.

questions.prompt: Ravi has 20 marbles and Asha has 15 marbles. Find the ratio of Asha's marbles to Ravi's marbles, in simplest form.
hints: Asha is named first, so start with Asha's 15 marbles: $15 : 20$.
Divide both terms by 5.
questions.solution: Asha to Ravi is $15 : 20$. Dividing both terms by 5 gives $3 : 4$.

questions.prompt: Which of these is the ratio of 9 to 4?
hints: "The ratio of 9 to 4" names 9 first, so 9 is the first term.
questions.solution: The ratio of 9 to 4 is written $9 : 4$.

questions.prompt: A recipe uses 2 cups of rice for every 3 cups of water. Write the ratio of rice to water.
hints: Rice is named first, so the cups of rice go first.
questions.solution: Rice to water is $2 : 3$.

objectives.title: Change both quantities to the same unit before writing a ratio

questions.prompt: Find the ratio of 50 paise to ₹ 2, in simplest form.
hints: ₹ 1 is 100 paise. How many paise is ₹ 2?
Now compare $50 : 200$ and simplify.
questions.solution: ₹ 2 is 200 paise, so the ratio is $50 : 200$. Dividing both terms by 50 gives $1 : 4$.

questions.prompt: Find the ratio of 30 minutes to 2 hours, in simplest form.
hints: 1 hour is 60 minutes. How many minutes are in 2 hours?
Compare $30 : 120$ and simplify.
questions.solution: 2 hours is 120 minutes, so the ratio is $30 : 120$. Dividing both terms by 30 gives $1 : 4$.

questions.prompt: Find the ratio of 600 g to 2 kg, in simplest form.
hints: 1 kg is 1000 g. How many grams is 2 kg?
Compare $600 : 2000$ and divide both terms by their HCF.
questions.solution: 2 kg is 2000 g, so the ratio is $600 : 2000$. Dividing both terms by 200 gives $3 : 10$.

questions.prompt: Find the ratio of 40 cm to 2 m, in simplest form.
hints: 1 m is 100 cm. How many centimetres is 2 m?
Compare $40 : 200$ and simplify.
questions.solution: 2 m is 200 cm, so the ratio is $40 : 200$. Dividing both terms by 40 gives $1 : 5$.

objectives.title: Write a ratio in its simplest form

questions.prompt: Write $24 : 36$ in simplest form.
hints: Find the HCF of 24 and 36.
The HCF is 12. Divide both terms by 12.

questions.prompt: Write $45 : 60$ in simplest form.
hints: Both numbers are in the 5 times table and the 3 times table.
The HCF of 45 and 60 is 15.

questions.prompt: Write $56 : 42$ in simplest form.
hints: Both numbers are in the 7 times table. Is there a larger common factor?
The HCF of 56 and 42 is 14.

questions.prompt: Write $1.5 : 2$ as a ratio of whole numbers in simplest form.
hints: Multiply both terms by 10 to remove the decimal: $15 : 20$.
Now divide both terms by their HCF.
questions.solution: Multiplying both terms by 10 gives $15 : 20$. Dividing both terms by 5 gives $3 : 4$.

objectives.title: Find equivalent ratios and a missing term

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: $2 : 3 = 8 : ?$
hints: What do you multiply 2 by to get 8?
Multiply 3 by the same number.
questions.solution: $2 \times 4 = 8$, so multiply 3 by 4 too: $3 \times 4 = 12$. So $2 : 3 = 8 : 12$.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: $5 : 4 = ? : 20$
hints: What do you multiply 4 by to get 20?
Multiply 5 by the same number.
questions.solution: $4 \times 5 = 20$, so multiply 5 by 5 too: $5 \times 5 = 25$. So $5 : 4 = 25 : 20$.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: $18 : 27 = 2 : ?$
hints: What do you divide 18 by to get 2?
Divide 27 by the same number.

questions.prompt: True or false: $3 : 5$ and $9 : 15$ are equivalent ratios.
hints: Is there one number you can multiply both 3 and 5 by to get 9 and 15?
questions.solution: True. Multiplying both terms of $3 : 5$ by 3 gives $9 : 15$.

objectives.title: Check whether four numbers are in proportion

questions.prompt: True or false: 3, 5, 12 and 20 are in proportion.
hints: Four numbers are in proportion when $3 : 5 = 12 : 20$.
Check whether the product of the extremes ($3 \times 20$) equals the product of the means ($5 \times 12$).

questions.prompt: True or false: 4, 6, 10 and 12 are in proportion.
hints: Compare $4 \times 12$ with $6 \times 10$.
If the two products are different, the numbers are not in proportion.
questions.solution: False. $4 \times 12 = 48$ but $6 \times 10 = 60$, so $4 : 6$ is not equal to $10 : 12$.

questions.prompt: True or false: 2, 7, 6 and 21 are in proportion.
hints: Compare $2 \times 21$ with $7 \times 6$.

questions.prompt: Which ratio is in proportion with $6 : 8$?
hints: Write $6 : 8$ in simplest form first.
$6 : 8 = 3 : 4$. Which option also simplifies to $3 : 4$?
questions.solution: $6 : 8 = 3 : 4$ and $9 : 12 = 3 : 4$, so $6 : 8$ and $9 : 12$ are in proportion.

objectives.title: Find the missing term of a proportion

questions.prompt: 4, 6, $x$ and 15 are in proportion. Find $x$.
hints: Write the proportion: $4 : 6 = x : 15$.
The product of the extremes equals the product of the means: $4 \times 15 = 6 \times x$.
questions.solution: $4 \times 15 = 6 \times x$, so $60 = 6x$ and $x = 10$.

hints: What do you multiply 3 by to get 15?
Multiply 8 by the same number.
questions.solution: $3 \times 5 = 15$, so $x = 8 \times 5 = 40$.

hints: The product of the extremes equals the product of the means: $5 \times 36 = x \times 20$.
$5 \times 36 = 180$. What times 20 makes 180?
questions.solution: $5 \times 36 = 20 \times x$, so $180 = 20x$ and $x = 9$.

objectives.title: Find the value of one item, then of many

questions.prompt: 6 notebooks cost ₹ 90. What is the cost of 1 notebook, in rupees?
hints: The cost of 1 notebook is less than the cost of 6. Should you multiply or divide?
Divide ₹ 90 by 6.
questions.solution: Cost of 1 notebook $= 90 \div 6 = 15$, so ₹ 15.

questions.prompt: 5 pens cost ₹ 60. How much do 8 pens cost, in rupees?
hints: First find the cost of 1 pen: $60 \div 5$.
1 pen costs ₹ 12. Now multiply by 8.
questions.solution: 1 pen costs $60 \div 5 = 12$ rupees, so 8 pens cost $12 \times 8 = 96$ rupees.

questions.prompt: A car travels 150 km on 10 litres of petrol. How far does it travel on 4 litres, in km?
hints: First find how far the car goes on 1 litre: $150 \div 10$.
The car goes 15 km on 1 litre. Now multiply by 4.
questions.solution: On 1 litre the car travels $150 \div 10 = 15$ km, so on 4 litres it travels $15 \times 4 = 60$ km.

questions.prompt: 12 workers are paid ₹ 3600 in total for a day's work. How much are 7 workers paid for a day, in rupees?
hints: First find what 1 worker is paid: $3600 \div 12$.
1 worker is paid ₹ 300. Now multiply by 7.
questions.solution: 1 worker is paid $3600 \div 12 = 300$ rupees, so 7 workers are paid $300 \times 7 = 2100$ rupees.

objectives.title: Use the unitary method to compare prices

questions.prompt: Which is the better buy? Pack A: 3 pencils for ₹ 15. Pack B: 5 pencils for ₹ 30.

options: Both cost the same per pencil

hints: Find the cost of 1 pencil in each pack.
Pack A: $15 \div 3$. Pack B: $30 \div 5$.
questions.solution: In Pack A one pencil costs $15 \div 3 = 5$ rupees. In Pack B it costs $30 \div 5 = 6$ rupees. Pack A is the better buy.

questions.prompt: A 5 kg bag of rice costs ₹ 260. What is the price of 1 kg, in rupees?
hints: The price of 1 kg is less than the price of 5 kg. Divide ₹ 260 by 5.
questions.solution: Price of 1 kg $= 260 \div 5 = 52$, so ₹ 52.

questions.prompt: Shop P sells 4 mangoes for ₹ 100. Shop Q sells 6 mangoes for ₹ 138. Which shop is cheaper per mango?
hints: Find the price of 1 mango at each shop.
Shop P: $100 \div 4$. Shop Q: $138 \div 6$.
questions.solution: At Shop P one mango costs $100 \div 4 = 25$ rupees. At Shop Q it costs $138 \div 6 = 23$ rupees. Shop Q is cheaper.
